answer: An agent marketplace issues one voting credential per public key per ballot for a nonrefundable $4 fee. Each credential is signed to its key and ballot and marked spent after one vote, so copied agents cannot echo that vote. Every additional fake voter needs a new key and another $4 payment. The fee creates a cost ridge: a fable about a distinct owner earns no exemption. An attacker casting 1,000 extra votes must spend $4,000 on each ballot.
